title: Brain-Aligned Multimodal LLMs for Social and Emotional Understanding of Cartoon Movies
abstract: arXiv:2610.22706v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer scalable annotations of social and affective content, but their temporal agreement with human judgments and neural predictive value require further evaluation. We compared diffusion-based and autoregressive MLLMs with continuous human Theory of Mind (ToM) and affective valence ratings across three short cartoon movies. Behavioral analyses assessed temporally aligned Pearson correlations, rating distributions, and the effects of preceding scene descriptions. Ratings from each source were separately used in subject-specific regression models to predict regional fMRI responses. Model ratings captured aspects of human temporal variation despite systematic distributional differences, with generally stronger alignment for valence than ToM. translated_title: 面向卡通电影社交与情感理解的脑对齐多模态大语言模型
translated_abstract: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）能够对社会和情感内容进行可扩展的标注，但其与人类判断在时间上的一致性以及对神经活动的预测价值仍需进一步评估。本研究将基于扩散模型和自回归架构的MLLMs与人类在三部短篇卡通电影上的连续心理理论（ToM）和情感效价评分进行了比较。行为分析评估了时间对齐的皮尔逊相关性、评分分布以及前置场景描述的影响。来自各来源的评分被分别用于被试特异性的回归模型中，以预测区域性fMRI响应。结果显示，尽管存在系统性的分布差异，模型评分仍能捕捉人类时间变化的某些方面，且对情感效价的对齐普遍强于对心理理论的对齐。前置语境在某些条件下能改善对齐效果，具体效果取决于模型和电影。在《The Present》这部影片中，更多脑区显示出对MLLM评分的显著编码（原文在此截断）。
tldr: 该研究比较了扩散型与自回归多模态大语言模型和人类在观看卡通电影时的心理理论与情感效价评分及fMRI脑响应，发现模型评分能捕捉人类的时间动态变化且与情感效价的对齐更好，并可作为特征有效预测多个脑区的神经活动。
en_tdlr: This study compares diffusion-based and autoregressive multimodal LLMs against continuous human Theory of Mind and affective valence ratings and fMRI responses during cartoon movie viewing, showing that model ratings capture human temporal dynamics with stronger alignment for valence and can effectively encode neural activity across multiple brain regions.
